prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1393; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two witnesses, along with photos from the scene. All sources agree the accident occurred as the claimant described it, and the other driver's account matches.

Entry 3: Inspected the damage to the claimant's vehicle. The location and severity of the damage are consistent with the impact described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's coverage start.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy. The police and witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision.

Entry 5: Received the medical records for the reported neck and back strain. The injury fits the type and force of the crash, and no prior injury to the same body area is known. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Each conversation with the claimant has produced the same account of the accident. Based on the evidence gathered so far, the claim is proceeding through standard handling with counsel as the point of contact.
